question.text: Which of the following entities is eligible to apply for registration as a KRA under SEBI KRA Regulations, 2011?

answer.text: A wholly owned subsidiary of a recognized stock exchange with a nationwide network of trading terminals

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI KRA Regulations specify that eligible applicants for KRA registration include a wholly owned subsidiary of a recognized stock exchange with a nationwide network of trading terminals, a wholly owned subsidiary of a depository or of any other SEBI-registered intermediary, and a wholly owned subsidiary of an SRO recognised by SEBI. The Trap: Option A (a SEBI-registered stock broker) is close but wrong. A broker itself cannot be a KRA; eligibility requires being a wholly owned subsidiary of an exchange, depository, other SEBI-registered intermediary or recognised SRO. Note: The 'wholly owned subsidiary' requirement is the common thread across all three eligible categories.
